mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above the 10-year monthly average predicts a near-term positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as investors anticipate accommodative policy sustaining equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 12-month rolling average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite FEDFUNDS above average, with p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test vs. pre-pause period.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a decline in UNRATE signals labor market strengthening, which reduces risk premia and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or statistically insignificant (p > 0.10) during the defined labor strength pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST (industrial production) of at least 2% above the prior quarter's average is associated with positive S&P 20-day forward returns via improved business optimism.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥2% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite qualifying HOUST growth, with p-value > 0.05 in a regression controlling for inflation and interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO below the 5-week moving average coincides with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as tight supply conditions raise financing costs for firms.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during INDPRO contraction, p > 0.10.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% in a single month, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to higher inflation expectations depressing equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05) during such CPI spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in UNRATE and a rise in PAYEMS over the next 5 months indicates improving labor market conditions, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while PAYEMS increases over the next 5 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or are statistically insignificant (p > 0.10) during the interaction pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in RSAFS (money demand) suggests reduced near-term spending, which predicts a negative S&P 5-day forward return as investors anticipate softer earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during sustained RSAFS declines.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 3% for two consecutive months in a tight-supply regime, S&P 60-day forward returns are expected to be positive due to lower borrowing costs easing supply-side constraints.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3% for two consecutive months and regime: tight supply
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not positive or are insignificant (p > 0.10) during qualifying UNRATE declines.
